Definition: to speak in a foreign tongue
BiblicalUsage: To speak a strange language appears once, in the exodus psalm in Psalms 114:1: "When Israel went out of Egypt, the house of Jacob from a people of strange language." The word marks the Egyptians as foreigners in speech, and Israel's going out as a going out from among strangers.
TheologicalSignificance: What convinces me is that this verse sets the exodus in one line: God's people left a land whose language was not theirs, and went out to hear the voice of their own God.
